title: Weekly Radar same-day latest successful update is canonical

riskAssessment.reason: The change alters same-date publication and replaces multiple mutually bound artifacts after an external Telegram side effect. The transaction must preserve the old canonical set on failure and recover without a second delivery.
riskAssessment.reviewedBy: Codex after the user's explicit acceptance of the same-day canonical update design

preReviewWarnings: Verify that no input snapshot is overwritten before Telegram succeeds.
Verify that same-day replacement is explicit at the archive API and that old four-artifact transactions remain recoverable.
Verify that schedule and workflow_dispatch use the same normal publication path while republish remains archive-neutral.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record checkpoints before implementation and finish to preserve scope and verification evidence.

acceptance: A normal same-day run from either schedule or workflow_dispatch may publish a new report instead of returning ALREADY-PUBLISHED before acquisition.
Only a successful Telegram delivery followed by a committed archive transaction makes the new report, rendered snapshot, receipt, manifest, and input snapshot the canonical same-day set.

A failed acquisition, rendering, Telegram delivery, transaction preparation, or partial commit leaves the prior canonical set intact or leaves a validated recoverable transaction that reuses the original receipt without a second Telegram send.

The strict creation API still rejects a different existing same-date input, --retry-as-of still rejects a completed final run, --verify-published-as-of creates no archive files, and --republish-published-as-of leaves report/snapshot/receipt/manifest bytes unchanged.
Existing four-artifact transaction records and pending recovery remain readable and fail closed on corruption or identity mismatch.
Automated tests cover same-day replacement, input snapshot binding, failure preservation/recovery, retry/verify/republish boundaries, and workflow branching.
User-facing Weekly Radar documentation explains manual triggering, last-successful-update canonicality, failure behavior, and the distinction between retry and republish.
No data ref, weekly-radar-pending ref, Secret, credential, or immutable predecessor archive is changed by this Work Item.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Do not import internal modules from other features.
Keep same-day replacement explicit and fail closed for incomplete or conflicting archive state.
Preserve the independent system-reference and human-judgment semantics in all user-facing wording.

intent.problem: A completed run currently makes all later same-day normal invocations stop before acquisition and Telegram. That prevents urgent manual execution and prevents a genuinely successful later update from becoming the day's canonical report. The old input snapshot is also written before Telegram, so simply allowing overwrite would risk binding an old report to a new input after a failed delivery.
constraints: The last successful same-day update is canonical; a failed attempt leaves the current canonical set.
Normal publication eligibility is identical for schedule and manual trigger.
Telegram success followed by archive or data publication failure remains recoverable without a second Telegram message.
Protected configuration and production ref edits are outside this Work Item.
Retry, verify, and explicit republish remain separate operations.
intent.rationale: An explicit replacement transaction lets the system prepare the new input in memory, send it, then commit all mutually bound artifacts together. This satisfies emergency manual execution while preserving fail-closed delivery recovery and historical identity checks.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A complete canonical run already exists and a normal same-day run succeeds.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The new successful report replaces the same-day report, snapshot, receipt, manifest, and input snapshot as one bound canonical set.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add a failing archive/CLI fixture that publishes two different inputs for one date, then assert the second manifest snapshot_id, report_id, receipt, and input snapshot all agree.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The new same-day attempt fails before or during archive commit.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The prior canonical files and input snapshot remain unchanged; a prepared transaction, if present, is recoverable and does not cause a second Telegram send.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Inject Telegram/transaction stage failures and compare all old bytes before recovery; then recover and verify the new five-artifact binding.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A normal workflow invocation is schedule or workflow_dispatch on a date with a final data run.
scenarioCoverage.expected: It enters normal acquisition/publication and does not use verify as an unconditional same-day no-op; explicit republish remains separate and archive-neutral.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Update workflow static assertions for the removed normal final-run verify branch and retained republish branch; run all workflow text tests.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Retry, verify, or explicit republish is invoked against a completed date.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Each operation keeps its existing boundary: retry does not overwrite a completed canonical run, verify is read-only, and republish sends without changing archive/data.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run existing and new CLI/fixture tests, including archive byte comparisons and explicit option validation.
